detail.title: Synthesis of Attractor Dynamics in Preference Formation
detail.summary: This research cycle synthesizes computational models of entorhinal cortex dynamics with interaction-driven attractor states to refine the theory of emergent preferences.

children.title: Interaction-Driven Attractor States as Stable Preferences

detail.title: Interaction-Driven Attractor States as Stable Preferences
detail.summary: Continuous attractor dynamics, supported by entorhinal grid-cell representations, provide a robust mechanism for generating stable, path-dependent preference states from continuous inputs.
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate new evidence on entorhinal cortical representations with existing attractor dynamics findings.
